decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm’s core integrated airport software offer and already has standalone visibility, so in a growing, investing firm with slack there is little reason to abandon it absent clear underperformance.

As an apron connectivity module that builds on established capabilities and fits the push toward digitally integrated operations, it is likely to be retained while management waits for results to settle.

Although it is related to the installed base, billing software is somewhat less central to the firm’s operational integration focus, so it faces a higher drop risk if early results fall short of aspirations, but current firm slack still favors retention.
Equipment monitoring software closely matches the firm’s engineering, maintenance, and analytics strengths, making it likely to stay on the market unless early feedback is clearly disappointing.
Apron resource management is near the firm’s existing airport operations portfolio and supports the strategy of end-to-end, data-driven efficiency, so management would likely continue it.
A controller safety alert service fits the firm’s safety-oriented airport systems business and should be kept while the firm uses its R&D and service capacity to refine and commercialize it.
